# Testing and markers

How to verify a server that cannot print, what the two kernel trace samplers do and do not catch,
the boot-marker-file contract, and the mutation-testing discipline. See
[`build-and-boot.md`](./build-and-boot.md) for the boot commands themselves (how to produce and time
a log) — this file covers how to read one.

## Verifying server behaviour

User-space servers run at EL0 with no console access — they cannot print. Verify server behavior
through kernel-side traces (`[pf]` from `do_page_fault`, `[ksys …]` from `do_vmctl`/`system`, `[ipc
N]` from `ipc::dispatch`), never server-side logging.

Trace sampling is asymmetric between the two: `[ipc N]` head-traces the first ~12 calls *plus* every
100th, but `[ksys N]` samples only every 100th (no head carve-out) — a server's first/rare kernel
call (e.g. a startup `SYS_GETINFO`) shows on `[ipc]`, not `[ksys]`.

The two `EFAULT` traces — `[efault] proc=… nr=… call=… va=…` and `[efault deliver] proc=… nr=… va=…`
— are **uncounted**, unlike the sampled `[ipc {n}]` form, which is what makes them stable boot
markers instead of ones that can fall out of a fixed-size sample window. The `do_ipc` one keys on
`result == EFAULT`, which is unambiguous because nothing else in the kernel produces that errno.
Keep that invariant in mind before changing `do_ipc`'s tracing — it's the thing that makes the
`[efault]` marker unambiguous.

## Trace forensics

The `[ipc]` modulo sampler almost never catches low-rate callers — a blocking SENDREC client (e.g. a
fork/wait loop) round-trips once per rotation, thousands of times rarer than a synchronous
kernel-call flood from a busier caller — and a server packed late in the MXBI archive boots after
that flood starts, so its SEF handshake never lands in `TRACE_HEAD` either.

**Zero sampled lines for such a caller is NOT evidence it's stuck.** Verify via its downstream
head-carved `[ksys …]` traces instead (e.g. `[ksys SYS_FORK]`/`SYS_EXIT` are head-carved at 6, so
raise the head const temporarily to count real cycles), or add a temporary unconditional `[DBG]`
trace in `ipc::do_ipc` keyed on the caller nr — remove it before committing.

## Exit-status probes

A process that cannot print at all — not even through a driver, e.g. `worker`'s exec-frame validator
running before a console exists — reports its verdict through its own exit status. **Encode the
pass, never the absence of a failure.** `execstack::EXEC_STACK_PROBE_PASS` (`0x5A`) is the positive
sentinel a passing probe returns; status `0` prints `FAIL no-verdict` rather than being read as
success, because two other paths can produce a `0` that means nothing:

- `mproc::handle_kill_in` zombifies a signalled process without touching `exit_status`, so a probe
  that died before it could report is reaped with status `0`.
- A frame bad enough to fault the probe lands it in VM's SIGSEGV arm, which prints no `!!! EL0 data
  abort` for the forbidden-marker list to catch — a silent, verdict-free death.

Companion rule: key any reap-derived marker on the child's **pid**, not on "the first reap" —
`alloc_pid` never returns `0`, so `0` is the correct "not yet" sentinel, and pid-keying is what
stops an unrelated zombie (reaped first, by the same parent) from being mistaken for the probe's own
child.

## Markers

`tools/check-boot-log.sh <log>` greps a captured boot log against `tests/qemu-boot.expected` /
`tests/qemu-boot.forbidden` (see [`build-and-boot.md`](./build-and-boot.md) for how to produce the
log and how long to budget). Update those marker files in the same PR when trace formats or the boot
roster change, or the `qemu-smoke` CI job goes red.

A few properties of the script matter when you're reading its output rather than just running it:

- **The marker files test first occurrences only**, never counts — keep expectations timing-robust,
  since CI's TCG is slower than local and a marker that only ever appears once is the only kind that
  survives that difference.
- **It works on a partial log.** Once it reports PASS on a still-growing log, the verdict is final
  and the boot can be stopped — the 5.10b review round got all 97 markers well inside the 600 s
  budget. Only `qemu-smoke`'s exit-124 assertion needs the timeout to actually elapse. Copy the log
  aside before checking; the live file grows underneath the script.

## VM: regions and unmapping

VM (`servers/vm/`) tracks per-process memory as a static `[ClientRegions; 16]` keyed by proc number
(no heap allocator — the kernel owns frames), each region a half-open `[start, end)` tagged

are Phase 4). `VM_BRK`/`VM_MMAP`/`VM_MUNMAP` all ride the single D→VM SENDREC edge, so adding an
mmap client needs no new priv wiring beyond the brk one.

`SYS_VMCTL(VMCTL_PT_UNMAP)` returns `EINVAL` (no panic, no frame freed) when nothing is mapped at
the target VA — so VM's `munmap` can sweep a region page-by-page with `VMCTL_PT_UNMAP` and ignore

## VM server region tracking

The VM server (`servers/vm/`) is the first real user-space process. It runs a `RECEIVE(ANY)` loop
and dispatches on message type. It owns no heap allocator — the kernel owns frames — so it tracks
memory with a static per-process region table (`servers/vm/src/region.rs`): `[ClientRegions; 16]`,
keyed by process number, each holding up to `MAX_REGIONS = 4` regions. A region is a half-open
virtual range `[start, end)` tagged with a `Kind`:

- `Heap` — grown by `brk`, based at the fixed `HEAP_BASE` (`0x0100_0000`).
- `Mmap` — anonymous mappings, bump-allocated from `MMAP_BASE` (`0x0200_0000`).
- `Unused` — a free slot.

(no heap allocator — the kernel owns frames), each region a half-open `[start, end)` tagged
`Kind::{Heap, Mmap, Unused}`. A page fault is satisfied only when its address lies inside a region;
out-of-region faults are a silent SIGSEGV (faulter left blocked on `RTS_PAGEFAULT` — real signals
are Phase 4). `VM_BRK`/`VM_MMAP`/`VM_MUNMAP` all ride the single D→VM SENDREC edge, so adding an
mmap client needs no new priv wiring beyond the brk one.

`SYS_VMCTL(VMCTL_PT_UNMAP)` returns `EINVAL` (no panic, no frame freed) when nothing is mapped at
the target VA — so VM's `munmap` can sweep a region page-by-page with `VMCTL_PT_UNMAP` and ignore
=== book memory:138-148 ===
## VM server region tracking

The VM server (`servers/vm/`) is the first real user-space process. It runs a `RECEIVE(ANY)` loop
and dispatches on message type. It owns no heap allocator — the kernel owns frames — so it tracks
memory with a static per-process region table (`servers/vm/src/region.rs`): `[ClientRegions; 16]`,
keyed by process number, each holding up to `MAX_REGIONS = 4` regions. A region is a half-open
virtual range `[start, end)` tagged with a `Kind`:

- `Heap` — grown by `brk`, based at the fixed `HEAP_BASE` (`0x0100_0000`).
- `Mmap` — anonymous mappings, bump-allocated from `MMAP_BASE` (`0x0200_0000`).
- `Unused` — a free slot.

Preserve these when extending the generator:

- Generated C uses **C11 keywords only** (`_Static_assert`, `_Alignas` on the struct's **first
  member** — C11 forbids `_Alignas` on a type declaration — and `_Alignof`) — never GNU attributes.
- `minixrs/ipc.h` **includes nothing**; `offsetof` comes from `__builtin_offsetof` under the private
  name `_MINIXRS_OFFSETOF`, because Apple's clang redirects `<stddef.h>` to the system header for
  any `*-musl` triple, which would break the hermetic `-nostdlibinc -ffreestanding` CI check.
- Every process gets **both** `<NAME>_PROC_NR` and `<NAME>_EP` — they differ for kernel tasks (e.g.
  `SYSTEM_PROC_NR` is −2, `SYSTEM_EP` is 32766) — and the header `_Static_assert`s the C decode
  macro against the Rust-computed endpoints.

1	# CI gates
2	
3	What runs on every PR, which gates block, and what to run locally before pushing. See
4	[`build-and-boot.md`](./build-and-boot.md) for the commands themselves.
5	
6	`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs on every PR and on pushes to `main`. Eleven gates run in parallel —
7	`fmt`, `clippy`, `clippy-kernel` (aarch64 kernel lint + compile), `c-headers` (regenerate + `clang
8	-fsyntax-only` the generated C ABI headers), `audit` (cargo-audit), `deny` (cargo-deny, config in
9	`deny.toml`), `dco` (DCO sign-off, PR-only), `geiger`, `miri`, `qemu-smoke` (aarch64 QEMU boot
10	smoke), `coverage` (cargo-llvm-cov → `lcov.info`) — then a `sonar` job feeds the LCOV report to
11	SonarQube Cloud (org `minixrs`, project `minixrs_minixrs`, config in `sonar-project.properties`).
12	The Sonar scan auto-detects PR vs branch: PRs get decoration, `main` pushes refresh the
13	whole-project picture.
14	
15	- Only `geiger` and `miri` are **advisory** (`continue-on-error`); the other nine block. miri only
16	  covers the host-testable crates (`-p minixrs-kernel-shared -p minixrs-vm -p minixrs-pm`) —
17	  `minixrs-ipc` has inline asm. `geiger`'s per-package sweep filters out `minixrs-kernel` (it can't
18	  host-build)
19	- The `clippy` job runs a **second `run:` step**, `cargo clippy -p minixrs-mfs --features server
20	  --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and it blocks like the first. It exists because `fs/mfs`'s
21	  `[[bin]]` carries `required-features = ["server"]`, so `main.rs` is **invisible to every other CI
22	  job** — clippy `--all-targets`, miri and llvm-cov all skip it without that feature. This step is
23	  the mitigation: without it the only thing in CI that compiles `fs/mfs/src/main.rs` at all is the
24	  `qemu-smoke` boot, which reports a lint failure as a mysterious build-script panic
25	- `dco` runs `tools/check-dco.sh <base>..<head>` and is **PR-only** (`if: github.event_name ==
26	  'pull_request'`): a push to `main` lands a GitHub merge commit, which by design has no sign-off,
27	  and the authored commits under it were already checked on their own PR. It needs `fetch-depth: 0`
28	  — the default shallow clone has neither endpoint of the range — and passes the two SHAs through
29	  `env:` rather than `${{ }}`-interpolating them into the `run:` (the standard expression-injection
30	  guard, kept even though these fields are hex). An **empty range is a failure, not a pass**: zero
31	  authored commits means the range was computed wrong, and a gate that greens on a broken range is
32	  worse than none. The script is bash 3.2-clean (no `mapfile`, no `${var,,}`) so it runs on a stock

      - run: cargo fmt --all --check

      # itself decides how config is resolved, so a floating CLI could still
      # move the output from under a checksum-pinned plugin. `dprint/check-action`
      # would do the same thing at the cost of another third-party action to
      # SHA-pin.
      - name: Install dprint (pinned)

      # home is only reachable while the pointers at it resolve. This checks that
      # every relative markdown link names a file that exists and, when it carries
      # a fragment, a heading that really renders to that anchor.
      - name: Check markdown links and anchors
        run: python3 tools/check-md-links.py
"""
assert old in s
p.write_text(s.replace(old, new, 1))
print("ok")

## Markdown formatting

All markdown in this repository wraps prose at **100 columns**. This is mechanical, not a habit.

Configuration is `dprint.json` at the repo root, pinning dprint-plugin-markdown by checksum. Tables,
fenced code blocks, and bare URLs are exempt — dprint leaves them alone. `<!-- dprint-ignore -->`
exempts the block that follows it.

**`textWrap: "always"` reflows a whole paragraph**, so consecutive lines separated only by a newline
are joined before being rewrapped. Anything that must keep its own line has to be a real markdown
block: a list item, a table row, or a paragraph separated by a blank line.

The installer puts the binary at `~/.dprint/bin/dprint`, which is **not** on `PATH` — use the
absolute path or add it.

**`grep -F` lies on formatted prose.** dprint wraps *inside* multi-word backticked tokens, so a
phrase that is present can still fail to match. Verify with whitespace normalised:

```bash
python3 -c "
import re,sys
norm=lambda s: re.sub(r'\s+',' ',s)
print(norm(sys.argv[1]) in norm(open(sys.argv[2],encoding='utf-8').read()))
" 'phrase to find' path/to/file.md
```

**A nested fence must be the last element inside its outer fenced block.** Prose after it makes
dprint close the outer fence early and strand that prose outside the block.

To prove a reformat changed no content, compare the **non-whitespace character sequence** before and
after. `git diff --ignore-all-space` is useless here: a reflow joins and splits lines, which git
sees as hundreds of changed lines.

Rust doc comments are out of scope — rustfmt does not reflow them and there is no gate that would.

```bash
dprint fmt          # format everything
dprint check        # verify, as CI will
```

Slice status is tracked as a GFM checkbox in the slice's own plan file, checked by the slice's own
PR. See [`git-and-prs.md`](./git-and-prs.md) for the full rule — this file does not restate it.

"""## One home is not enough: the pointers have to land

Every rule in this tree has exactly **one** home, and every other file that needs it links there
instead of restating it. Deduplicating is only half of that contract, and it is the half that is
easy to check. The other half is that the links still arrive at the section holding the rule — and a
dedupe pass that verifies only single-ownership will pass a tree full of pointers into nothing.

This has now failed twice in the same week, both times found by a reviewer rather than by the sweep
that had just declared the tree clean: a confused-deputy link into `abi.md` that resolved to a file
with no such rule in it, and slice 5.9's back-link that resolved to the right file but the wrong
section. In both cases the rule *did* have one home. Nothing pointed at it.

So the check is two questions, not one:

1. Does this rule appear in exactly one place?
2. Does every reference to it resolve to **that place** — right file, right section?

Question 2 is mechanical and `tools/check-md-links.py` answers it: every relative markdown link
names a file that exists, and every `#fragment` names a heading that really renders to that anchor.
It runs in CI's `fmt` job and blocks. Run it locally after any move, rename, or dedupe:

```bash
python3 tools/check-md-links.py
```

**Do not hand-roll an anchor slugger instead.** Three separate attempts in this repository got
GitHub's rules wrong and reported working links as broken — collapsing runs of whitespace (GitHub
emits one hyphen per space), stripping `_` (GitHub keeps it, so `#…sys_diagctl` and `#naked-_start…`
are correct), and scanning line by line (dprint reflows prose, so a link's `[label]` and its
`(target)` routinely land on different lines). Acting on any of those first runs would have
"repaired" links that already worked. The script encodes all three corrections.

Question 1 stays manual, and the trap there is the fix itself: consolidating a rule into one section
and then *summarising it* at the old site recreates the duplicate under a different wording, which
drifts faster than a verbatim copy would. The old site gets a sentence naming the rule and a link —
never a paraphrase of what the rule says.

markdown fails the PR the same way unformatted Rust does.""")

**Goal (as written 2026-08-04):** the tracker still labelled 5.11 `◀ ready (pending merge)` after PR

what came next.

**Outcome:** resolved by removing the class of defect rather than the instance. PR #58 replaced the
`◀ next` / `◀ ready` / `✓ shipped (PR #N, merged …)` marker vocabulary with a **GFM checkbox checked
by the PR that does the work**, so a slice can no longer be described as complete by a later
documentation pass, and "what is next" is read off the first unchecked box instead of a marker
somebody has to remember to move. The retired-form `✓ shipped` lines on the Phase 2–5 slices stay as
history; no new one is ever written.

Nothing further is owed here. The Phase 6 checkboxes already exist, unchecked, in
[`../plan.md`](../plan.md).

## Chunk 2: User VA map — high stack, larger stack, image-relative brk — [ ]

**Do this before any virtio code.** Phase 5 kept a greenfield *low* map that is not borrowed from
32-bit MINIX 3 (which puts `USR_STACKTOP` near `0xF0000000`). Verified on `main`:

| VA            | Role                                                                      | Defined in                                |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `0x0010_0000` | load base (`user.ld` / clang `--image-base`)                              | `user.ld`, LLVM patch 0006                |
| `0x0020_0000` | **one** stack page (`SERVER_STACK_VA`) — a 1 MiB image ceiling            | `kernel/src/arch/aarch64/userland.rs:149` |
| `0x0100_0000` | fixed `HEAP_BASE` (brk)                                                   | `servers/vm/src/region.rs:36`             |
| `0x0200_0000` | mmap bump arena (`MMAP_BASE`)                                             | `servers/vm/src/region.rs:50`             |
| `0x4000_0000` | device window (TTY UART; Phase 6 virtio-mmio pages) — also `REGION_LIMIT` | `kernel-shared/src/uspace.rs`             |
| `0x8000_0000` | ramdisk window                                                            | `kernel-shared/src/uspace.rs`             |

Four consequences, all of which Phase 6 makes worse:

1. **Image ceiling.** Any `PT_LOAD` reaching `0x200000` collides with the stack (`AlreadyMapped` /
   exec `ENOMEM`). Multi-MiB disk-resident programs are exactly what Phase 6 invites, and tooling's
   risk register already tracks this.
2. **One-page stack.** `SERVER_STACK_BYTES == USER_PAGE_SIZE == 4096`, unchanged by the stretch
   slices — which instead added pressure: MFS carries **two** 4 KiB `.bss` buffers (`BLOCK` and
   5.10b's `STAGE`) and VFS a 256 KiB `EXEC_STAGE`, all `.bss` precisely because a one-page stack
   cannot hold them. VirtIO descriptor rings and bounce buffers hit the same wall.
3. **Fixed heap origin.** `HEAP_BASE` is unrelated to the last loaded segment. musl malloc
   eventually needs a real `brk`/`mmap`; opening USER→VM without fixing the map cements the wrong
   layout.
4. **The clang pin is compensating for the OS.** LLVM patch 0006 forces `--image-base=0x100000`
   because lld's aarch64 default *is* `0x200000` — the stack. Relocating the stack is the OS-side
   fix the tooling docs deferred to "a later minixrs slice".

**Scope:**

- **High stack.** Map the initial stack near the top of user VA, clear of the device
  (`0x4000_0000`) and ramdisk (`0x8000_0000`) windows. Prefer a MINIX-shaped `USR_STACKTOP`-style
  constant in `kernel-shared::uspace` so tooling's `check-image.sh` can share it. Note
  `userland.rs`'s `const _` assert that the device window sits above `SERVER_STACK_VA + PAGE_SIZE`:
  a high stack **inverts** that guard, so rewrite it rather than delete it.
- **Grow the stack.** Raise `SERVER_STACK_BYTES` to several pages, for servers and for exec'd
  images. Revisit MFS's two `.bss` buffers and VFS's stage — a local becomes viable again; keep
  `fs/mfs`'s `const _` tripwire honest. musl's `%Lf` VLAs (~7.4 KiB) were already a landmine at
  4 KiB.
- **brk after the last `PT_LOAD`.** Drop the fixed `HEAP_BASE` for exec'd (and eventually boot)
  images: the loader reports image-end, VM seeds the heap region at `[page_align_up(image_end), …)`
  or defers creating it until the first `VM_BRK`. Stub D / boot-stubs need a migration story or stay
  on a legacy origin behind the `boot-stubs` feature.
- **mmap arena.** Keep it bumping above the heap, or place it in a high hole below the stack; still
  capped at `REGION_LIMIT` (the lowest kernel-owned window, `USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_BASE`).
- **`Kind::Stack` (optional).** Track the stack as a VM region so fork clones it and fault
  accounting stays consistent — today the kernel maps the page and VM never hears about it.
- **Tooling sync.** Update tooling's `verify/check-image.sh` VA constants in the **same** change
  window, and decide whether clang may drop the unconditional `--image-base` pin (keep it if a
  shared `0x100000` load base independent of the stack is still wanted).

**Proof:** a multi-MiB image loads and runs; `sp` is high in the `[exec] … sp=0x` marker (which is
prefix-only today — good); brk lands past the last `PT_LOAD`; tooling's image checker is green.
Re-mutation-test the image-base and oversized-image fixtures. This is a **mandatory** three-boot
matrix change — see [`ci.md`](../conventions/ci.md#the-sdk-flavor-has-zero-ci-coverage).

**Out of scope:** CoW, ASLR, guard-page stack growth, and USER→VM for malloc — the last can follow
immediately once the map is sane.

## Chunk 3: `SYS_IRQCTL` design note — [ ]

**Goal:** Phase 6's first real kernel work is IRQ delivery to EL0 (a `NOTIFY` from `HARDWARE` after
registration). `stubs::do_irqctl` is still `ENOSYS`, dispatched from `kernel/src/system/mod.rs`.
Write the design note **before** coding virtio-blk.

**Scope** — a section in the Phase 6 tracker (chunk 4) covering:

- register / unregister / enable / disable subcodes;
- privilege (`k_call_mask`): which drivers may claim which IRQs;
- masking while a NOTIFY is in flight (MINIX's storm avoidance);
- GIC routing on QEMU `virt` for virtio-mmio IRQs;

  TTY refuses it from its unknown-request arm, so RX is **one new arm in TTY** with no VFS or ABI
  change.

**Do not** invent a one-off "poll forever in the driver" for blk. TCG may hide the latency, but the
milestone is a disk root under real completion interrupts.

**Proof:** the note exists and 6.1 implements it; a single forced-IRQ round trip is visible as a
`[diag]` line or a boot marker before any virtio code is written.

## Chunk 4: Phase 6 tracker + slicing session — [ ]

**Goal:** [`../plan.md`](../plan.md)'s Phase 6 is five checkboxes and one milestone, and there is no
`docs/plans/phase-6-*.md`. That is exactly how Phase 5 looked before `phase-5-prep.md` chunk 6
produced [`phase-5-musl-fs.md`](phase-5-musl-fs.md). **This chunk gates starting Phase 6 proper.**

**Scope:** add `docs/plans/phase-6-virtio.md` with locked decisions and a per-slice scope/proof
table, linking to the `docs/superpowers/{specs,plans}/` documents rather than restating them (see
[`docs-and-workflow.md`](../conventions/docs-and-workflow.md)).

**Recommended decomposition** (adjust freely):

| Slice   | Goal                                                  | Observable proof                                                                         |
| ------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **6.0** | User VA map — chunk 2, if it has not already landed   | Multi-MiB image loads; `sp` high; brk past the last `PT_LOAD`; tooling checker green     |
| **6.1** | `SYS_IRQCTL` + HARDWARE NOTIFY                        | Driver registers a line; a forced IRQ reaches it; storm-safe masking                     |
| **6.2** | `driver-rt` VirtIO MMIO transport + virtqueues        | Enumerate a virtio device; feature bits; read back a known config field                  |
| **6.3** | `virtio-blk` behind BDEV                              | MFS root works with MEM *or* virtio selected; read **and write** markers identical       |
| **6.4** | GPT / `mkimage.sh` + Limine + a MinixFS partition     | QEMU `-drive if=virtio`; boots without the MXBI `rootfs` (or with it as fallback)        |
| **6.5** | TTY RX and/or virtio-console                          | TTY serves `CDEV_READ`; optional shell prep for Phase 7                                  |
| **6.6** | virtio-net, packet I/O only                           | TX/RX frames in diag; no TCP                                                             |

Landing IRQCTL + virtqueues + blk + disk image + console RX in one PR would recreate the pain
Phases 4–5 avoided. `tools/` has no `mkimage.sh` today.

## Chunk 5: musl syscall surface — [ ]

**This is the widest gap between what the kernel can do and what C can reach**, and the stretch
slices widened it. `external/musl`'s `src/minixrs/_syscall.c` still dispatches exactly six Linux
call numbers: `writev`, `write`, `exit`, `exit_group`, `set_tid_address`, `ioctl`.

- **A C program cannot open, read, or write a file.** Everything 5.8–5.10b built (`VFS_OPEN` /
  `VFS_READ` / `VFS_WRITE` / `VFS_CLOSE`, `FS_CREATE`, `FS_TRUNC`) is exercised only by the Rust
  `init` probes, and `/dev/null` and `/dev/zero` are likewise unreachable from C.
- `hello` needs no malloc — `mmap` and `brk` are link stubs. The first non-`hello` C program on disk
  needs both malloc *and* file I/O.

**Scope**, after chunk 2 and before any C beyond `hello`:

- `openat` / `read` / `close` / `lseek`-shaped wrappers onto VFS. The fd numbering already matches:
  VFS `NR_FDS = 8`, with 0/1/2 pre-opened to the console.
- Real `brk` / `mmap` / `munmap` onto VM — widening USER's `ipc_to` to include VM, **with the
  reverse reply edge**; the 5.4 lesson is that each entry costs a *pair* of bits.
- Re-verify musl's `__init_tls` and arena assumptions against the new heap origin.
- **D8 applies.** Any new request number or payload field is an ABI bump touching both repos, and
  the fork branch is force-pushed — so the fork bump and the `external/musl` submodule bump land in
  the **same** PR. See [`abi.md`](../conventions/abi.md).

**Proof:** a C program that opens a file on the MinixFS root, reads it, and prints its contents —
through musl, not through an `init` probe.

## Chunk 6: SDK flavor CI coverage — [ ]

`MINIXRS_SDK` appears **zero** times in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, so the SDK `hello` flavor is
never exercised on a runner and a patched-clang-driver regression ships green. Markers are
byte-identical across the SDK and musl flavors, which is what makes this invisible.

**Scope:** an SDK-cached CI job, or an explicit decision to keep the gap and rely on the local
three-boot matrix. The rule and the full local mitigation live in
[`ci.md`](../conventions/ci.md#the-sdk-flavor-has-zero-ci-coverage) — this file does not restate
them.

---

## Sequencing: keep the ramdisk until virtio-blk is green

D3's contract is that **Phase 6 swaps virtio-blk under an unchanged MFS.** Until blk passes the same
BDEV self-check battery MFS already runs — now including the **write** path (`fs.write ok n=32768
v=32768`, create/truncate, the `/etc/holey` hole probe) — keep packing `rootfs` and booting the MEM
backend. Dual-backend selection (boot arg, DS name, or a compile-time feature) beats a flag day that
blacks out every FS marker at once. The bar rose with 5.10: a read-only virtio backend is **no
longer** marker-equivalent to MEM.

## Capacity: what is already raised, and what is not

| Limit                                    | Value             | Note                                                                           |
| ---------------------------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `NR_SERVED_PROCS`                        | 32                | The shared PM/VM/SCHED ceiling — keep it shared                                |
| VM `MAX_REGIONS`                         | 16                | Already raised from the Phase-4 "4" scare                                      |
| VFS `NR_FDS`                             | 8                 | Raised 4 → 8 in 5.8; VFS-local, not ABI                                        |
| `SERVER_STACK_BYTES`                     | 4 KiB             | **Raise in chunk 2** — three large `.bss` buffers exist only because of it     |
| `ROOTFS_IMAGE_BLOCKS` / `ROOTFS_NINODES` | 256 (1 MiB) / 128 | Fine for the ramdisk; a disk root must not inherit either as a format limit    |
| qemu-smoke budget                        | 600 s             | Raised 120 → 240 → 600 across 5.10a/5.10b; disk I/O under TCG will push again  |

Before raising the boot budget again, measure the way [`ci.md`](../conventions/ci.md) prescribes —
the last required marker's byte position as a fraction of a fixed-timeout log, compared against the
same number at the merge base — and think in the *ratio*, not the wall-clock seconds.

## Carried from Phase 5: two unproven write-back orderings

5.10a and 5.10b left two write-back orderings **correct but unproven by any boot marker**. Probe
them in whatever slice adds `lseek` or a second truncate consumer; the detail is in
[`phase-5-musl-fs.md`](phase-5-musl-fs.md).

## Explicit non-goals for the pre-6 window

- Do **not** remove the MXBI `rootfs` ramdisk on day one of Phase 6.
- Do **not** couple "first virtio boot" to "full Unix VA map" in one PR — land chunk 2 first, so a
  disk bring-up failure is not also a layout failure.
- Do **not** write inside `$MINIXRS_SDK` when adjusting image-base or stack assumptions: tooling's
  `build-musl.sh` still does `rm -rf $SDK/sysroot`.
- Do **not** reopen the D8 ABI freeze for convenience. `0x700..0xC00` has been **fully allocated**
  (PM / VFS / FS / BDEV / CDEV) since 5.8, so a Phase 6 band needs a home outside that span.

## Deferred: do not block Phase 6 on these

| Item                               | Why it can wait                                            |
| ---------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SENDA` + `trap_mask: u32`         | musl uses SENDREC; the README already qualifies the claim  |
| `SYS_TIMES`                        | Nice for `time(1)`; not needed for a disk boot             |
| CoW fork                           | Performance, not correctness                               |
| PFS / pipes                        | Phase 7 shell                                              |
| Indirect grants                    | No re-granting consumer yet                                |
| Signal dispositions / `SIGCHLD`    | Shell / job control                                        |
| Orphan reparent to init            | Multi-process userland                                     |
| `GETDENTS` / `stat` on the FS band | No consumer until a shell lists a directory                |
| Dynamic linking                    | Far future                                                 |
| x86_64                             | Phase 8                                                    |

---

## One-line summary

Phase 5 and its three stretch slices delivered a read-write POSIX data path and device nodes on a
ramdisk — but only to Rust callers. Before Phase 6 grows device windows and multi-MiB disk programs,
replace the temporary low-stack / fixed-heap map with a high stack, a larger stack, and an
image-relative brk; then slice IRQCTL → virtio transport → blk-under-BDEV → real disk image, keeping
the ramdisk until the new backend is marker-green, and widen the musl syscall surface so C can reach
the filesystem that already works.

+image-relative brk; then slice IRQCTL → virtio transport → blk-under-BDEV → real disk image, keeping

lines: -# Pre–Phase 6 Recommendations
-**Date:** 2026-09-17 (revalidated; first written 2026-08-04) **Scope:** Review of Phases 0–5 as
-shipped on `main` **through PR #57 / slice 5.11** — i.e. the milestone-B Phase 5 *and* all three
-post-milestone stretch slices — before starting Phase 6 (VirtIO drivers + root on disk).
-**Sources:** `docs/plan.md`, `docs/plans/phase-5-musl-fs.md`, CLAUDE.md conventions, `RECOMMEND.md`
-(the Phase-4 → 5 predecessor), tree inventory, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, and the live boot marker
-set in `tests/qemu-boot.expected` (86 expected + 20 forbidden).
-This is not a redesign of Phase 6. It is a checklist of **soft-ground risks**, **high-value
-cleanups**, and **sequencing advice** so virtio-blk / IRQ / disk root do not land on scaffolding
-that Phase 5 deliberately left temporary.
-Companion: `RECOMMEND.md` was the same genre before Phase 5. Most of its blockers (grants,
-fault-safe copy, TTY, VFS, MFS, musl) are now done. What remains below is what Phase 5 *explicitly
-deferred* plus debt that virtio will make expensive.
-> **Revalidation note (2026-09-17).** The 2026-08-04 draft assumed 5.10 and 5.11 were unstarted.
-> Both shipped (5.10a PR #53, 5.10b PR #54, 5.11 PR #57), so §3.1 and §3.2 are now *history*, not
-> recommendations. **Everything in §2 — the VA map, the one-page stack, the fixed heap origin, the
-> `SYS_IRQCTL` stub — was re-checked against the tree today and is unchanged.** The stretch slices
-> added no new fixed VA and did not move `SERVER_STACK_BYTES`; if anything they made the stack item
-> worse (§2.1). One genuinely new gap surfaced: the musl fork's syscall surface has not grown with
-## 1. Where things actually are
-### Milestone status
-| Phase                    | Plan claim                 | Reality on `main`                                                                                                    |
-| 0–4                      | complete                   | Done                                                                                                                 |
-| **5 – musl + FS**        | **complete** (milestone B) | **Done** — PR #52 (slice 5.9) merged 2026-08-04                                                                      |
-| 6 – VirtIO + disk root   | next                       | **Not started** — `drivers/virtio-{blk,console,net}/src/main.rs` are 5 lines each; `driver-rt/src/lib.rs` is 4 lines |
-**Bottom line:** Phase 5's bar — C `Hello from C!` via musl, **exec'd from `/bin/hello` on the
-MinixFS ramdisk**, through VFS → MFS → BDEV(`memory`) → grants → TTY — is met, and the ramdisk
-filesystem is now **read-write** (write, create, truncate) with `/dev/null` and `/dev/zero` served
-as CDEV minors. The boot-archive `hello` module is gone on purpose so the five C markers *are* the
-exec-from-FS proof. `worker` stays MXBI-embedded as the name-form / exec-stack regression.
-### What is solid
-- **Cross-AS data path:** PT-walk `uaccess`, grants (direct + magic), `SYS_COPY` / `SYS_SAFECOPY` /
-  `SYS_SETGRANT`, confused-deputy discipline (`m_source`, never payload granter).
-- **Console path:** user-space TTY (TX-only PL011), CDEV, VFS write, `SYS_DIAGCTL` for server debug.
-- **Block + FS path:** BDEV → `memory` ramdisk → MFS (**read *and* write**: data writes, zone
-  allocation, `FS_CREATE`, `FS_TRUNC`) → VFS open/read/write/close with `O_CREAT`/`O_TRUNC`; fixed 1
-  MiB / 256-block, 128-inode `rootfs` in MXBI, with sparse-file support in `mkfs-mfs`.
-- **Device nodes:** `/dev/null` + `/dev/zero` as `memory` CDEV minors 3 and 5; `CDEV_READ` defined;
-  VFS's three-row device-node table resolved ahead of the mount.
-- **Exec:** SysV initial stack + auxv; name-form *and* grant-sourced `SYS_EXEC`; PM/VFS staging;
-  `/bin/hello` from MFS.
-- **C ABI:** musl fork @ v1.2.6, generated headers, ABI freeze (D8), three-way hello flavor (SDK /
-  musl / worker) with musl as qemu-smoke's real path.
-- **Toolchain:** `aarch64-unknown-minixrs` brand, SDK flavor (`$MINIXRS_SDK`), clang driver pins
-  (`-z` flags, `--image-base=0x100000`).
-- **CI:** blocking qemu-smoke (**600 s** budget after 5.10b, `timeout-minutes: 50`), clippy-kernel
-  both feature configs, c-headers, DCO, etc.
-### What is intentionally skeletal (by design)

-| Component                                              | State                                                                                                                                                                  | Owner phase                             |

-| `SYS_IRQCTL`                                           | still `ENOSYS` (`system/stubs.rs`)                                                                                                                                     | **6** (hard gate for RX / virtqueues)   |

-| TTY RX                                                 | absent — `CDEV_READ` now *exists* and TTY answers it from its unknown-request arm (`ENOSYS`)                                                                           | **6** (adds one TTY arm; VFS untouched) |

-| `drivers/virtio-*`, usable `driver-rt`                 | placeholders (5 / 4 lines)                                                                                                                                             | **6**                                   |

-| **musl syscall surface**                               | six arms only: `writev`, `write`, `exit`, `exit_group`, `set_tid_address`, `ioctl`. **No `openat`/`read`/`close`** — so the FS work of 5.8–5.10b is unreachable from C | **pre-6 / early 6** (see §3.3)          |

-| PFS / pipes                                            | out of Phase 5                                                                                                                                                         | **7**                                   |

-| `SENDA`                                                | denied (`trap_mask: u16`) + `ENOSYS`                                                                                                                                   | non-goal                                |

-| CoW fork                                               | eager copy                                                                                                                                                             | later                                   |

-| Signal handlers / async `SIGCHLD` / orphan reparent    | default-terminate + wait-reap only                                                                                                                                     | later                                   |

-| USER → VM `ipc_to` / real `mmap`/`brk` for musl malloc | stubs / fixed `HEAP_BASE`                                                                                                                                              | **pre-6 layout work** (below)           |

-| Disk image / `mkimage.sh` / GPT                        | missing (`tools/` has no `mkimage.sh`)                                                                                                                                 | **6**                                   |

-| SDK flavor CI coverage                                 | zero — `MINIXRS_SDK` appears **0** times in `ci.yml`                                                                                                                   | tooling / CI                            |
-*(Retired from this table since 2026-08-04: MFS write / `BDEV_WRITE`-answers-`EROFS`, shipped as
-5.10a/5.10b; `/dev/null` + `/dev/zero`, shipped as 5.11.)*
-### Doc freshness (do immediately)
-The 5.9 marker has been flipped, but the footgun simply moved: **`docs/plan.md:538` and
-`docs/plans/phase-5-musl-fs.md:1557` still label 5.11 as `◀ ready (branch
-feature/slice-5.11-dev-null-zero, pending merge)`** although PR #57 merged on 2026-09-06. There is
-now **no `◀ next` marker anywhere in `docs/`** — the tracker does not say what comes next at all.
-**Recommend:** flip 5.11 → `✓ shipped (PR #57, merged 2026-09-06)` in both files, state that the
-Phase 5 stretch set is complete, and place `◀ next` on Phase 6 (or on the named pre-6 layout slice
-## 2. Do these before (or as the first slices of) Phase 6
-*Re-verified 2026-09-17 against the tree: every constant below is unchanged since the 2026-08-04
-draft.*
-### 2.1 User VA map: high stack + image-relative brk — **do before virtio**
-Phase 5 kept a **greenfield low map** that is *not* borrowed from 32-bit MINIX 3 (MINIX uses
-`USR_STACKTOP ≈ 0xF0000000`). Today:
-| VA            | Role                                                                      | Defined in                                |
-| `0x0010_0000` | load base (`user.ld` / clang `--image-base`)                              | `user.ld`, LLVM patch 0006                |
-| `0x0020_0000` | **one** stack page (`SERVER_STACK_VA`) — **1 MiB image ceiling**          | `kernel/src/arch/aarch64/userland.rs:149` |
-| `0x0100_0000` | fixed `HEAP_BASE` (brk)                                                   | `servers/vm/src/region.rs:36`             |
-| `0x0200_0000` | mmap bump arena (`MMAP_BASE`)                                             | `servers/vm/src/region.rs:50`             |
-| `0x4000_0000` | device window (TTY UART; Phase 6 virtio-mmio pages) — also `REGION_LIMIT` | `kernel-shared/src/uspace.rs:69`          |
-| `0x8000_0000` | ramdisk window                                                            | `kernel-shared/src/uspace.rs:90`          |
-Consequences that Phase 6 will make worse:
-1. **Image ceiling.** Any `PT_LOAD` that reaches `0x200000` collides with the stack (`AlreadyMapped`
-   / exec `ENOMEM`). Tooling's risk register already tracks this; multi‑MiB disk-resident programs
-   are exactly what Phase 6 invites.
-2. **One-page stack.** `SERVER_STACK_BYTES == USER_PAGE_SIZE == 4096`
-   (`kernel-shared/src/uspace.rs:122`) — unchanged by the stretch slices, which instead *added*
-   pressure: MFS now carries **two** 4 KiB `.bss` buffers (`BLOCK` + 5.10b's `STAGE`,
-   `fs/mfs/src/main.rs:142,156`) and VFS a 256 KiB `EXEC_STAGE`, all `.bss` precisely because a
-   one-page stack cannot hold them. VirtIO drivers with descriptor rings / bounce buffers will hit
-   the same wall.
-3. **Fixed heap origin.** `HEAP_BASE` is unrelated to the last loaded segment. musl malloc
-   eventually needs a real `brk`/`mmap` path; opening USER→VM without fixing the map just cements
-   the wrong layout.
-4. **Clang pin is compensating for the OS.** LLVM patch 0006 forces `--image-base=0x100000` because
-   lld's aarch64 default *is* `0x200000` (the stack). Relocating the stack is the OS-side fix the
-   tooling docs deferred to "a later minixrs slice."
-**Recommend a dedicated pre-Phase-6 slice** (name it e.g. `5.12` / `pre6-uspace` / `6.0-layout` —
-whatever keeps plan markers honest) that lands the Unix-ish map **before** virtio-mmio premapping
-proliferates:

-| Change                       | Detail                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

-| **High stack**               | Map the initial stack near the top of user VA (or well above every growing region and below `USER_VA_TOP`), clear of the device (`0x4000_0000`) and ramdisk (`0x8000_0000`) windows. Prefer a MINIX-shaped `USR_STACKTOP`-style constant in `kernel-shared::uspace` so tooling/`check-image.sh` can share it. Note `userland.rs:172`'s `const _` asserts the device window sits above `SERVER_STACK_VA + PAGE_SIZE`; a high stack inverts that guard, so rewrite it rather than delete it. |

-| **Grow stack size**          | Raise `SERVER_STACK_BYTES` to multiple pages (servers and exec'd images). Revisit MFS's two `.bss` buffers and VFS's stage — a local becomes viable again; keep `fs/mfs`'s `const _` tripwire honest. Exec stack for musl/`%Lf` VLAs (~7.4 KiB) was already a known landmine at 4 KiB.                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

-| **brk after last `PT_LOAD`** | Drop fixed `HEAP_BASE` for exec'd (and eventually boot) images: loader reports image-end; VM seeds the heap region as `[page_align_up(image_end), …)` (or defers creation until first `VM_BRK`). Stub D / boot-stubs need a migration story or stay on a legacy origin behind `boot-stubs`.                                                                                                                                                                                                |

-| **mmap arena**               | Keep bump-above-heap or place it in a high hole below the stack; still capped at `REGION_LIMIT` (= lowest kernel-owned window, i.e. `USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_BASE`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

-| **Kind::Stack (optional)**   | Track the stack as a VM region so fork clones it and fault/accounting stay consistent — today the kernel maps the page and VM never hears about it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

-| **Tooling sync**             | Update `tooling`'s `verify/check-image.sh` VA constants in the **same** change window; decide whether clang may drop the unconditional `--image-base` pin (keep it if you still want a shared `0x100000` load base independent of stack).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

-| **Markers**                  | `[exec] … sp=0x` is prefix-only today — good. Re-mutation-test image-base / oversized-image fixtures.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
-**Why before virtio, not "with disk boot":** virtio-mmio will add more device window pages and
-possibly new premaps; every new fixed VA makes a later layout migration harder. Stack/heap reshaping
-is **orthogonal** to ramdisk→virtio-blk (D3: MFS stays unchanged under a new BDEV backend). Do
-layout first, then swap the block device.
-**Out of scope for that slice:** CoW, ASLR, growable stacks via guard pages, USER→VM for malloc (can
-follow immediately after once the map is sane).
-### 2.2 `SYS_IRQCTL` design note — **blocker for any RX / virtqueue**
-Phase 6's first real kernel work is IRQ delivery to EL0 (`NOTIFY` from `HARDWARE` after register).
-Today `stubs::do_irqctl` is still `ENOSYS` (`kernel/src/system/stubs.rs:25`), dispatched from
-`system/mod.rs:262`.
-**Recommend:** before coding virtio-blk, write a short design note (even a section in
-`docs/plans/phase-6-*.md`) covering:
-- register / unregister / enable / disable subcodes
-- privilege (`k_call_mask`) — which drivers may claim which IRQs
-- masking while a NOTIFY is in flight (MINIX storm avoidance)
-- GIC routing on QEMU `virt` for virtio-mmio IRQs
-- how TTY RX and virtio-console share the pattern — 5.11 already shaped this: `CDEV_READ` exists and
-  TTY refuses it from its unknown-request arm, so RX is **one new arm in TTY** with no VFS or ABI
-  change
-Do not invent a one-off "poll forever in the driver" for blk; TCG may hide latency, but the
-milestone is disk root under real completion interrupts.
-### 2.3 Slice Phase 6 the way 2–5 were sliced — **process**
-`docs/plan.md` Phase 6 is still five bullets + one milestone, and there is no
-`docs/plans/phase-6-*.md`. That is how Phase 5 looked before chunk 6 produced `phase-5-musl-fs.md`.
-Since 5.10a the per-slice design + plan documents also land in `docs/superpowers/{specs,plans}/`; a
-Phase 6 tracker should link to those the way the Phase 5 one does rather than restate them.
-**Recommended decomposition** (adjust freely):
-| Slice          | Goal                                                           | Observable proof                                                                         |
-| **pre6 / 6.0** | User VA: high stack + larger stack + image-relative brk (§2.1) | Multi‑MiB image loads; `sp` high; brk past last `PT_LOAD`; tooling checker green         |
-| **6.1**        | `SYS_IRQCTL` + HARDWARE NOTIFY                                 | Driver registers line; forced IRQ → `[diag]` / marker; storm-safe mask                   |
-| **6.2**        | `driver-rt` VirtIO MMIO + virtqueues                           | Enumerate a virtio device; feature bits; ping a known config field                       |
-| **6.3**        | `virtio-blk` behind BDEV                                       | MFS root still works with MEM *or* virtio selected; read **and write** markers identical |
-| **6.4**        | GPT / `mkimage.sh` + Limine + MinixFS partition                | QEMU `-drive if=virtio`; boot without MXBI `rootfs` (or with it as fallback)             |
-| **6.5**        | TTY RX and/or virtio-console                                   | TTY serves `CDEV_READ`; optional shell-prep for Phase 7                                  |
-| **6.6**        | virtio-net (packet I/O only)                                   | TX/RX frames in diag; no TCP yet                                                         |
-Trying to land IRQCTL + virtqueues + blk + disk image + console RX in one PR will recreate the pain
-Phases 4–5 avoided.
-### 2.4 Keep the ramdisk until virtio-blk is green — **sequencing**
-D3's contract: **Phase 6 swaps virtio-blk under an unchanged MFS.** Until blk passes the same BDEV
-self-check battery MFS already runs — now including the **write** path (`fs.write ok n=32768
-v=32768`, create/truncate, the `/etc/holey` hole probe) — keep packing `rootfs` and booting MEM.
-Dual-backend selection (boot arg / DS name / compile-time feature) beats a flag day that blacks out
-every FS marker. Note the bar rose with 5.10: a read-only virtio backend is no longer
-marker-equivalent to MEM.
-## 3. Strongly recommended stretch / early Phase 6 adjacent
-### 3.1 ~~Slice 5.10 — MFS write path~~ — **shipped**
-Landed as **5.10a** (PR #53, 2026-08-20: `BDEV_WRITE` stores for real, `FS_WRITE`, `VFS_WRITE` to
-files, zone allocation with bitmap-before-pointer ordering) and **5.10b** (PR #54, 2026-09-02:
-`FS_CREATE`/`FS_TRUNC`, `VFS_OPEN` flags, the staging-buffer invariant that closed 5.10a's mid-write
-zone leak). Two write-back orderings remain *correct but unproven* by any boot marker — see the
-5.10a/5.10b notes in CLAUDE.md; probe them in whatever slice adds `lseek` or a second truncate
-consumer.
-### 3.2 ~~Slice 5.11 — `/dev/null` + `/dev/zero`~~ — **shipped**
-Landed as PR #57 (2026-09-06), and it cost one new *request* after all: `CDEV_READ` (the "new
-minors, not new requests" prediction in the 5.3 notes was wrong for reading zero, and was corrected
-in-tree). Also delivered VFS's device-node table and a real `CDEV_READ` path to TTY for
-`/dev/console`.
-### 3.3 musl wrappers — **now the widest gap between kernel and C**
-This is the item the stretch slices *widened*. `external/musl`'s `src/minixrs/_syscall.c` still
-dispatches exactly six Linux call numbers — `writev`, `write`, `exit`, `exit_group`,
-`set_tid_address`, `ioctl`. So:
-- **A C program cannot open, read, or write a file.** Everything 5.8–5.10b built
-  (`VFS_OPEN`/`READ`/`WRITE`/`CLOSE`, `FS_CREATE`, `FS_TRUNC`) is exercised only by the Rust `init`
-  probes. `/dev/null` and `/dev/zero` are likewise unreachable from C.
-- `hello` still needs no malloc (`mmap`/`brk` are link stubs). The first non-hello C program on disk
-  will need both malloc *and* file I/O.
-**Recommend**, after §2.1 and before any C beyond `hello`:
-- `openat` / `read` / `close` / `lseek`-shaped wrappers → VFS (fd numbering already matches: VFS
-  `NR_FDS = 8`, fds 0/1/2 pre-opened to the console)
-- real `brk` / `mmap` / `munmap` → VM (widen USER `ipc_to` to include VM, with reverse reply edges —
-  the 5.4 lesson: each entry costs a *pair* of bits)
-- re-verify musl `__init_tls` / arena assumptions against the new heap origin
-- remember D8: any new request number or payload field is an ABI bump touching both repos, and the
-  fork branch is force-pushed, so the fork bump and the `external/musl` submodule bump land in the
-  **same PR**
-### 3.4 Capacity (mostly already raised)

-| Limit                                    | Value                             | Note                                                                                                                                                                                    |

-| `NR_SERVED_PROCS`                        | 32                                | Shared PM/VM/SCHED ceiling — keep it that way                                                                                                                                           |

-| VM `MAX_REGIONS`                         | **16**                            | Already raised from the Phase-4 "4" scare in `RECOMMEND.md`                                                                                                                             |

-| VFS `NR_FDS`                             | **8**                             | Raised 4 → 8 in 5.8; VFS-local, not ABI                                                                                                                                                 |

-| `SERVER_STACK_BYTES`                     | **4 KiB**                         | **Raise in §2.1** — and now three large `.bss` buffers exist because of it                                                                                                              |

-| `ROOTFS_IMAGE_BLOCKS` / `ROOTFS_NINODES` | 256 (1 MiB) / 128                 | Fine for ramdisk; disk root should not inherit either as a format limit                                                                                                                 |

-| qemu-smoke budget                        | **600 s** (`timeout-minutes: 50`) | Raised 120 → 240 → 600 across 5.10a/5.10b. Disk I/O under TCG will push again — measure the last marker's byte fraction against the merge base, per CLAUDE.md, and think in the *ratio* |
-### 3.5 SDK CI gap
-Still **zero** CI coverage of the `$MINIXRS_SDK` hello flavor — `MINIXRS_SDK` appears nowhere in
-`.github/workflows/ci.yml`. Markers are byte-identical across SDK/musl, so a clang driver regression
-can ship green. Until an SDK-cached job exists, keep the local three-boot matrix when touching
-`build_hello*` / driver flags — and treat an image-base / stack move as a **mandatory** matrix run
-(§2.1 is exactly that kind of change). Remember `MINIXRS_SDK` does not persist across separate shell
-invocations: check the embedded `hello` size (~200 KB musl, ~47 KB SDK, ~15 KB fallback) rather than
-trusting the build warning.
-## 4. Nice-to-have; do not block Phase 6
-| Item                               | Why defer                                                |
-| `SENDA` + `trap_mask: u32`         | musl uses SENDREC; marketing already qualified in README |
-| `SYS_TIMES`                        | nice for `time(1)`; not needed for disk boot             |
-| CoW fork                           | performance, not correctness                             |
-| PFS / pipes                        | Phase 7 shell                                            |
-| Indirect grants                    | no re-granting consumer yet                              |
-| Signal dispositions / `SIGCHLD`    | shell / job control                                      |
-| Orphan reparent to init            | multi-process userland                                   |
-| `GETDENTS` / `stat` on the FS band | no consumer until a shell lists a directory              |
-| Dynamic linking                    | far future                                               |
-## 5. Suggested first two weeks
-1. **Docs:** flip the 5.11 markers in `docs/plan.md` and `docs/plans/phase-5-musl-fs.md`; place `◀
-   next`; add `docs/plans/phase-6-virtio.md` with locked decisions + slice table (§2.3).
-2. **Layout slice (§2.1):** high stack, multi-page stack, brk after last `PT_LOAD`; sync tooling
-   checkers; boot matrix (SDK / musl / worker, default + `--no-default-features`).
-3. **IRQCTL design + stub→real** as 6.1, with a single forced-IRQ proof before any virtio code.
-4. **Only then** grow `driver-rt` and `virtio-blk` behind BDEV beside MEM.

-to `brk`.)

-- Do **not** remove the MXBI `rootfs` ramdisk on day one of Phase 6.

-  bring-up failures are not also layout failures.
-- Do **not** write inside `$MINIXRS_SDK` when adjusting image-base / stack assumptions (tooling's
-  `build-musl.sh` still `rm -rf $SDK/sysroot`).
-- Do **not** reopen D8 ABI freeze for convenience; new bands/calls need a deliberate ABI bump
-  touching the musl fork. Note `0x700..0xC00` is **fully allocated** (PM/VFS/FS/BDEV/CDEV) since 5.8
-  — a Phase 6 band needs a home outside that span.
-## 7. One-line summary
-Phase 5 plus its three stretch slices delivered a read-write POSIX data path and device nodes on a
-ramdisk — but only to Rust callers. Before Phase 6 grows device windows and multi‑MiB disk programs,
-**replace the temporary low stack/fixed-heap map with a high stack, larger stack, and image-relative
-brk**; then slice IRQCTL → virtio transport → blk-under-BDEV → real disk image, keeping the ramdisk
-until the new backend is marker-green, and widen the musl syscall surface so C can actually reach
-the filesystem that already works.

(slice 5.1, D2 — see [phase-5-musl-fs.md](../plans/phase-5-musl-fs.md))

Three rules were written out in full in two files apiece, which is how the

  samplers' asymmetry -- stood in both testing-and-markers.md and

  in ci.md; that home is testing-and-markers.md.

it is `[ClientRegions; MAX_CLIENTS]` with `MAX_CLIENTS = NR_SERVED_PROCS` (32),
and the 16 is `MAX_REGIONS`, a different axis.

Consolidating a rule and then paraphrasing it at the old site would recreate the
duplicate under new wording, so each old site gets a link, never a summary.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

git add .github/workflows/ci.yml tools/check-md-links.py docs/conventions/docs-and-workflow.md CLAUDE.md && git commit -q --signoff -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
ci: block on markdown formatting and link integrity

dprint has been the markdown formatter since PR #58 but nothing enforced it, and
nothing at all checked that a cross-reference still lands where the rule lives.
Both now run as steps of the existing `fmt` job rather than as new jobs: neither
needs a build, and a twelfth blocking job would cost a runner for two seconds of
work. The job keeps the CI name `rustfmt` because that is what branch protection
requires.

dprint's CLI version is pinned in the workflow alongside the plugin checksum
already pinned in dprint.json -- the checksum constrains the plugin, not how a
floating CLI resolves config.

tools/check-md-links.py is the second half of the one-home rule. Deduplicating a
rule is easy to verify; that the pointers still arrive at it is the half that
gets skipped, and it has now failed twice in a week, both times caught by a
reviewer rather than by the sweep that had just called the tree clean. The
script answers it mechanically: every relative link names a file that exists,
and every #fragment names a heading that really renders to that anchor.

Three corrections are baked in, each of which a hand-rolled generator in this
repository got wrong and each of which reports working links as broken:

- one hyphen per space, never collapsed;
- `_` is preserved, so #...sys_diagctl and #naked-_start... are correct;
- scan the document, not line by line -- `textWrap: "always"` reflows prose, so
  a link's [label] and its (target) routinely land on different lines.

Verified armed, not just green: a deliberately broken same-file anchor and a
deliberately broken cross-file anchor both fail the check, and the tree is clean
at 288 links across 39 files.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)" && git log --oneline -4 && git status --short && echo "--- final verification ---" && ~/.dprint/bin/dprint check && python3 tools/check-md-links.py && cargo fmt --all --check && echo "clean"

content.text:
All four items are done on `chore/pre6-cleanup` — 4 commits, all GPG-signed and DCO-clean. Nothing pushed; the branch is waiting for your approval.

**The dprint gate.** `dprint check` plus `tools/check-md-links.py` now run as steps of the existing `fmt` job, not as new jobs — neither needs a build. The job keeps the CI name `rustfmt` because that's what branch protection matches; rename it only together with the protection rule. The dprint *CLI* is pinned to 0.57.4 in the workflow, since the plugin checksum in `dprint.json` constrains the plugin but not how a floating CLI resolves config.

**The six follow-ups.** `CDEV_WRITE`'s payload doc now explains the 12..16 padding the way every sibling offset constant already did. The 5.0 record names `_MINIXRS_OFFSETOF` and says the 5.6 sweep renamed it. `[ClientRegions; 16]` was two numbers stale in `servers-and-drivers.md` and `book/` — it's `MAX_CLIENTS` (32) with `MAX_REGIONS` at 16; `phase-3-vm.md` keeps the old numbers because they're accurate history for slice 3.5. The three duplications each have one home now, with links replacing the copies.

`RECOMMEND.md` turned out not to be in the repo at all — it's excluded via `.git/info/exclude`, so that dead citation was only ever in your working tree. I fixed it there anyway; it's untracked, so it isn't in any commit.

**One home vs. pointers that land.** The rule is written into `docs-and-workflow.md`, and the checker makes half of it mechanical. Two things worth your attention:

The checker's first run reported four broken anchors in `docs/plans/`. All four were my generator stripping `_`, for the third time in this work. Had I acted on that run I'd have "fixed" four links that already worked. It also initially missed a genuinely broken anchor, because it scanned line by line and `textWrap: "always"` had split that link across two lines. Both corrections are in the script, and I verified it fails on a deliberately broken same-file and cross-file anchor rather than only confirming it passes.

Then the dedupe itself produced exactly the defect it was meant to prevent: moving the `diag_print` text out of `servers-and-drivers.md` left `kernel.md` pointing at a file that no longer held it. The link resolved — it had no fragment — so the checker couldn't catch it. That's the residual gap: a bare file link can rot without breaking.

**`PRE6-RECOMMEND.md`** is landed as `docs/plans/phase-6-prep.md`, six chunks in `phase-5-prep.md`'s shape. I re-checked every constant against `main` before carrying it — the one-page stack, fixed `HEAP_BASE`, `do_irqctl`'s `ENOSYS`, musl's six syscall arms, the 5-line virtio placeholders, `MINIXRS_SDK` at zero occurrences in `ci.yml` — all still hold. The marker item is chunk 1, marked done: PR #58 removed the marker vocabulary rather than fixing the instance, and I kept the reasoning since it explains why the convention changed. The draft moved to the scratchpad at `.../scratchpad/PRE6-RECOMMEND.md` rather than being deleted.

Local gates green: `cargo fmt`, workspace clippy, MFS clippy, kernel clippy both configs, `kernel-shared` tests, `cargo gen-c-headers` wrote nothing into the tree. QEMU smoke I have not run — it's the 600 s boot, and nothing here touches code paths it exercises.
